title: Ike's Morning Digest
data_note: Built from publisher RSS metadata (titles + teaser text). `coverage_window_hours` is the default (40h); several feeds use a longer `rollingHours` (see `scripts/build-digest.mjs`) so rows align with what is still on each publisher’s listing pages. Commercial Observer keeps its retail category + hub supplement; TRD adds a New York–filtered global retail tag feed. PincusCo uses the live site feed only (`/category/retail/feed/` is stale). **CRE Daily** retail briefs come from `credaily.com/sectors/retail/feed/`. Open each link for the full article (subscriptions may apply in the browser).

section_overviews.commercial_observer:
Zara Doubles Footprint at a Macerich Shopping Center in Los Angeles County: Fashion firm Zara is more than doubling its footprint at a Southern California shopping center. The clothing retailer is expanding from 22,000 square feet to a 45,000-square-foot flagship opening next year at Macerich ’s 1.3 million-square-foot Los Cerritos Center in southeast Los Angeles County.

Municipal Credit Union Signs 6K-SF Lease for New Branch at 162-15 Jamaica Avenue: Municipal Credit Union (MCU) has signed a lease to open a new retail branch in Jamaica, Queens, Commercial Observer has learned. The not-for-profit credit union, which has locations citywide and caters only to New York City residents, signed a 15-year, roughly 6,000-square-foot lease at Michael Rosilio ’s 162-15.

Happier Grocery to Open Second NYC Location on the Upper East Side: A healthy grocery retailer is opening its second New York City location on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. Happier Grocery has signed a 20,500-square-foot lease at CSC Real Estate ’s 210 East 86th Street , where it plans to open a health food store like its original one on Canal Street in the second half of 2027,.

Sephora’s Meatpacking District Store Relocates to 401 West 14th Street: Beauty retailer Sephora is taking a walk up the block to 401 West 14th Street . The makeup giant has signed a 4,200-square-foot deal with landlords Taconic Partners and Nuveen Real Estate to relocate its Meatpacking District store one block north from 21-27 Ninth Avenue , according to the landlords.
section_overviews.cre_daily:
Invesco REIT Buys Raleigh Retail Center for $87.2M: Invesco REIT acquired Knightdale Marketplace for $87.2M, including closing and leasing costs, according to AltsWire. The 323,113 SF shopping center is 100% leased with a weighted average lease term of about seven years.

Core Retail Sales Hit Record as In-Store Spending Rises: Core retail sales rose 1.2% in August and 5.6% year over year, with gains across nine of 10 major retail categories. Store-based sales increased 0.6%, outpacing headline inflation and marking the second-largest monthly gain in the past 14 months.

Mall Values Jump 13% as Retail Recovery Accelerates: Green Street says mall values increased 13% over the past year, the strongest gain among 10 commercial property sectors. Limited new supply, resilient consumer spending and tenant upgrades have supported occupancy, rent growth and investor interest.

Restaurant Traffic Falls 2.4% Across US in August: US dining visits fell 2.4% year over year in August, reversing gradual improvement recorded in June and July. Overall retail visits still rose 0.3%, but growth slowed sharply from 1.7% in July.
section_overviews.new_york_post:
Rams turning rundown mall into new 52-acre, $10 billion village HQ with thousands of homes planned: Permanent construction is targeted for 2027, with the broader neighborhood expected to be built out in phases spanning roughly a decade.

Baby Boomers are pouring into Eastern seaboard state — rejecting cities’ unaffordable taxation: Baby Boomers are moving to the first state's beach towns for low taxes and coastal living, fueling new construction, higher home prices and growing pains.

Massive Northern California vineyard goes up for sale after Canada booze ban: A massive family-run California winery has fallen victim to Canada’s ban on booze imports — listing 11 vineyards amounting to 3,500 acres for sale as a wave of bankruptcies and closures rock the industry.

NYC gets crushed in affordability ranking for renters — but nearly tops the list for 1 huge perk: Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens rank near the bottom of RentCafe’s 2026 best cities for renters list as high housing costs drag down NYC.

items.headline: Zara Doubles Footprint at a Macerich Shopping Center in Los Angeles County
items.summary: Fashion firm Zara is more than doubling its footprint at a Southern California shopping center. The clothing retailer is expanding from 22,000 square feet to a 45,000-square-foot flagship opening next year at Macerich ’s 1.3 million-square-foot Los Cerritos Center in southeast Los Angeles County. Zara’s existing store will remain open during construction. The property is at 239 Los Cerritos Center near the border between L.A. and Orange counties.…

items.headline: Municipal Credit Union Signs 6K-SF Lease for New Branch at 162-15 Jamaica Avenue
items.summary: Municipal Credit Union (MCU) has signed a lease to open a new retail branch in Jamaica, Queens, Commercial Observer has learned. The not-for-profit credit union, which has locations citywide and caters only to New York City residents, signed a 15-year, roughly 6,000-square-foot lease at Michael Rosilio ’s 162-15 Jamaica Avenue , according to landlord broker Augenbaum Realty . Asking rent for the ground-floor space in Jamaica’s business district was more than $100 per square foot, according to the brokerage.…

items.headline: Invesco REIT Buys Raleigh Retail Center for $87.2M
items.summary: Invesco REIT acquired Knightdale Marketplace for $87.2M, including closing and leasing costs, according to AltsWire. The 323,113 SF shopping center is 100% leased with a weighted average lease term of about seven years. The REIT raised $79.2M quarter to date through August, nearly double the $46.2M reported through July. Key Takeaways AltsWire reports that Invesco Real Estate Income Trust bought the Raleigh-area retail center for $87.2M.…

items.headline: Core Retail Sales Hit Record as In-Store Spending Rises
items.summary: Core retail sales rose 1.2% in August and 5.6% year over year, with gains across nine of 10 major retail categories. Store-based sales increased 0.6%, outpacing headline inflation and marking the second-largest monthly gain in the past 14 months. Preliminary Q3 2026 data showed positive net absorption across single- and multi-tenant retail, with supply roughly in line with demand. Key Takeaways Consumer spending strengthened broadly in August, supporting both online and physical retail.…

items.headline: Mall Values Jump 13% as Retail Recovery Accelerates
items.summary: Green Street says mall values increased 13% over the past year, the strongest gain among 10 commercial property sectors. Limited new supply, resilient consumer spending and tenant upgrades have supported occupancy, rent growth and investor interest. Major owners including URW and CBL are increasing exposure again, although mall values remain below their decade-ago peak. Key Takeaways The Wall Street Journal reports that malls have become the top-performing commercial real estate sector after years of distress.…

items.headline: Restaurant Traffic Falls 2.4% Across US in August
items.summary: US dining visits fell 2.4% year over year in August, reversing gradual improvement recorded in June and July. Overall retail visits still rose 0.3%, but growth slowed sharply from 1.7% in July. September traffic will help show how much of August’s restaurant weakness came from calendar timing versus softer demand. Key Takeaways GlobeSt reports that US dining visits fell broadly in August while retail traffic remained slightly positive .…

items.headline: Nomic AI Inks 5K-SF Deal at 99 University Place Near Union Square
items.summary: Four tenants have signed office deals adding up to 15,593 square feet at a 10-story office building near Manhattan’s Union Square , Commercial Observer has learned. Design software firm Nomic AI , therapy space provider Therapeutic Alliance Suites and construction systems developer T Moriarty & Son each signed 4,890-square-foot leases across full floors of Bijan Nassi ’s 99 University Place , according to landlord broker Noah & Co. Asking rent in the building is $55 per square foot, Noah & Co. said.…

items.headline: Conduct AI Takes 7K SF at Capstone’s 140 Crosby Street for First U.S. Office
items.summary: A London-based artificial intelligence firm developing enterprise software is establishing its first U.S. office presence in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. The rapidly growing Conduct AI has signed a 6,705-square-foot lease on the entire third floor of 140 Crosby Street , owned by Capstone Equities , Rugby Realty and Republic Investment Company , according to landlord broker JLL . JLL did not immediately disclose the length of the lease or the rent involved.…

items.headline: Distyl AI Doubles Its 135 Madison Offices to 30K SF After Less Than a Year
items.summary: Software development company Distyl AI has room to grow. The artificial intelligence-powered developer of operating systems for large companies has leased the entire ninth floor at 135 Madison Avenue in Manhattan’s NoMad neighborhood, according to building manager Koeppel Rosen , bringing the company’s total footprint to 30,076 square feet.…

items.headline: Irish Arts Center Signs 4K-SF Lease at GFP’s 630 Ninth Avenue
items.summary: GFP Real Estate has signed three new office deals at its Film Center Building in Hell’s Kitchen. The largest of the leases at 630 Ninth Avenue was for the Irish Arts Center , the corporate entity of which is known in the Hibernian tongue as An Claidheamh Soluis , which signed a three-year, 4,422-square-foot lease on the 14th floor of the building while its permanent location at 553 West 51st Street is redeveloped, according to GFP.…

items.headline: Toys R Us Plans 120 Holiday Stores in Retail Push
items.summary: Toys R Us plans 120 temporary standalone stores for the holiday season, compared with 36 permanent US locations. The pop-ups expand a 2023 strategy that used 24 temporary stores, while the brand also adds airport and shop-in-shop formats. National retail vacancy was 4.2% at the end of June, with limited new construction keeping available space relatively tight. Key Takeaways Toys R Us is preparing a major temporary store expansion for the holiday season.…

items.headline: The C-PACE Opportunity for Ground-Leased Properties
items.summary: Ground leases underlie some of the country’s most valuable commercial real estate. They are common in high-value markets such as Manhattan and are frequently used when land is owned by a university, public authority, institution or large corporate entity. They can also provide the long-term site control needed for projects involving new market tax credits or historical tax credits while allowing the landowner to retain fee ownership.…

items.headline: Asian-American Deli Café Hestia Signs 8K-SF Lease at 570 Lexington Avenue
items.summary: A cafe serving Asian and American cuisine is opening a fourth Manhattan location, Commercial Observer has learned. Café Hestia , a group of family-run delis, has signed a 20-year, 8,000-square-foot lease at the base of the Feil Organization ’s 570 Lexington Avenue , which it will likely also use as a catering facility, according to tenant broker Kassin Sabbagh Realty (KSR).…

items.headline: Stroller Brand Uppababy Relocates Store to 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights
items.summary: Known for its distinctive strollers, baby gear brand Uppababy is relocating its store within Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. The high-end baby accessories brand is opening a 3,780-square-foot brick-and-mortar location at Owen Realty ’s 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights, according to broker JLL . Uppababy will move next year from 90 Smith Street in Cobble Hill, where it established its Brooklyn retail and service “hub” in about 2019.…

items.headline: Harbor Fitness to Open 20K-SF Club at 3460 Nostrand Avenue in South Brooklyn
items.summary: Harbor Fitness has signed a lease for its eighth location in Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. The Brooklyn-based fitness brand signed a 25-year, 20,000-square-foot lease at Gaama Partners ’ 3460 Nostrand Avenue , according to broker Augenbaum Realty . The space was divided evenly between the first floor and the lower level of the property in Sheepshead Bay, Brooklyn. Asking rent for the space was $40 per square foot, according to the brokerage.…

items.headline: Two Supermarkets Ink Deals Along Brooklyn’s Atlantic Avenue
items.summary: Two new supermarkets are coming to Atlantic Avenue in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn. The grocers will arrive at two of EMP Capital Group ’s newly developed residential projects two blocks apart at 880 Atlantic Avenue and 1042 Atlantic Avenue , Commercial Observer has learned. In the largest deal, CTown Supermarkets signed a 20-year lease for 8,400 square feet at the base of the 19-story, 237-unit 1042 Atlantic Avenue, also known as Prosper Brooklyn , which was completed this year.…

items.headline: Wellness Tenants Emerge as New Retail Traffic Anchors
items.summary: Fitness, recovery, spa, and health concepts are increasingly functioning as primary traffic anchors for retail properties. Health and beauty locations have nearly doubled since 2018, expanding at an 8.4% annual rate, according to Newmark. Recurring memberships, frequent visits, and hospitality-driven design are strengthening the real estate case for wellness tenants. Key Takeaways Health and wellness concepts are moving from niche tenants to primary retail traffic drivers, Newmark wrote.…

items.headline: In Los Angeles Retail, a Widening Divide
items.summary: Los Angeles remains a locale that runs on ambition and the pursuit of opportunity. But a significant bifurcation is taking place. Increasingly, the marketplace for retail real estate has significantly split between those benefiting from buoyant dynamics and tenants whose small business dreams are starting to evaporate.…

items.headline: Market Shifts, New York’s Uniqueness Mean Mamdani’s Grocery Plan Could Work
items.summary: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani wants to get the city into the subsidized grocery business. As his administration seeks a seasoned partner this fall to run its planned quintet of government-supported grocery stores, strong opposition means it won’t sail through the express checkout lane. Plus, a pair of new lawsuits could stop the scheme faster than you can cancel an Instacart order, and many critics decry the initiative as the first step in a descent into socialism.…
